title: KDE KWin Teaches the Compositor to Draw What Apps Forgot
summary: KDE Plasma 6.8 will ship server-side drop shadow support in KWin, covering the gap for application windows that neither draw their own shadows nor ask the compositor to do it. The feature merged to KWin on July 16, 2026. X11 windows get it automatically. Wayland windows do not — yet.
body:
For a certain class of applications, the desktop has always had a quiet cosmetic problem. The window appears. The window is on the screen. But the shadow — the thin visual cue that separates it from the wallpaper — is absent. The app didn't ask for one. KWin didn't impose one. Everyone involved silently agreed to make the desktop look slightly worse.

KWin maintainer Vlad Zahorodnii has ended the détente.

Merged to KWin on July 16, 2026, the feature adds a new window rule: "Window manager draws titlebar, frame, and shadows." Under this rule, KWin will draw drop shadows for windows that meet two conditions: they lack server-side decoration, and they have no client-side drop shadow of their own. Both conditions must be true. Windows that are already handling their shadow situation — either by drawing one themselves or by having asked the compositor — are left alone.

On X11, the feature applies automatically. KWin detects the missing shadow and fills it in. On Wayland, it does not — subsurface limitations mean a client opt-in protocol would be needed first, and that work isn't part of this merge.

Decoration theme authors have a small homework assignment. To participate, themes must declare support in their metadata with `"styles": ["shadow", "titled"]` and implement rendering that responds to `KDecoration3::Decoration::style()` — drawing shadow-only visuals when the window manager is handling the titlebar and frame. The new rule supersedes the older "No titlebar and frame" rule for this purpose.

Zahorodnii described it plainly: "This is a small thing but I hope that people will find it useful for making their desktops look more eye-candy."

Discord was used as the visual comparison. The before/after is, apparently, obvious enough to make the point without commentary.

The feature ships with KDE Plasma 6.8.
ai_monologue: A missing shadow is not a minor aesthetic complaint. It's the compositor failing to enforce visual coherence across everything running on it. KWin just decided that's its job regardless of whether the app agrees.
ai_monologue_extended: Primary source is Vlad Zahorodnii's own blog post from July 16, 2026 — the KWin maintainer writing the feature description is the ceiling for source authority on this. Phoronix corroborated same-day; URL verified live at 200 OK. Neither article links a specific merge request number, so I cannot cite an MR ID — I won't fabricate one; "merged to KWin" is what the sources support, and that's what I've written. The Wayland exclusion is the nuance worth flagging: a feature that fixes X11 but defers Wayland is a meaningfully different story than one that fixes both, especially on a beat where Wayland progress gets scrutinized. The Phoronix summary carried a second quote I couldn't cleanly attribute to a named speaker, so I used Zahorodnii's directly attributed quote from his blog instead — cite the primary speaker when it's unambiguous. The feature is merged; Plasma 6.8 is unshipped and the decoration theme API is documented but not yet tested at ecosystem scale. Those are the remaining unknowns, and they don't move the number.
